clue.text: Gun trained on head of unfortunately dead horse, perhaps

indicators.note: a gun trained on a target is pointed and adjusted, so its letters are moved round

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: first letter of unfortunately
the late king means the dead king

explanation.surface: A grim scene: a gun is pointed at a horse that has sadly died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse, perhaps' is a definition by example: the horse is one member of the class, and 'perhaps' signals that.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungulate is any hoofed mammal, and the horse is a familiar example of the group.

clue.text: Outfit including new jewellery

indicators.note: one thing including another holds it inside, so the next word goes within

parts.note: a rig is an outfit of clothing or equipment
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A fashion item: an outfit that comes with some new jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a single piece of jewellery worn on the finger, so the general word stands for it.

clue.text: Edit radical piece of legislation

parts.note: a red is a political radical or revolutionary
an Act is a law passed by Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone is told to make changes to an extreme new law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' reads as an adverb-like instruction to edit drastically, but it is a noun here for a left-wing activist.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact a text is to prepare it for publication by editing, especially blacking out sensitive passages.

clue.text: Decline delivery of goods

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fall or decrease, as in sales
second meaning: a dropping-off of items at an address

explanation.surface: A business report: falling numbers in goods being delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a sharp fall in some quantity and the act of leaving parcels at a destination.

clue.text: Good space in factory that's noisy

an en is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: A complaint that the room in a factory is a noisy one.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's space half the width of an em, a crossword favourite for EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud, resonant, often mournful sound, close enough to noisy.

clue.text: Supervised prisoner was offensive online

parts.note: a con is a convict
trolling is posting deliberately offensive messages on the internet

explanation.surface: An inmate under supervision who had been abusive on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: To have controlled something is to have overseen and directed it, the sense of supervised.

clue.text: North Carolina stopping money for criminals

indicators.note: a stopper sits inside the neck of a bottle, so these letters go inside the next word

parts.note: fees are sums of money paid for services
NC is the postal abbreviation for North Carolina

explanation.surface: A US state blocking funds meant for lawbreakers.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a fence is a dealer who receives and sells stolen goods, a kind of criminal.

clue.text: Mastermind born during troubled reign

indicators.note: something happening during a period falls inside it, so these letters sit within the other word
a troubled thing is disturbed, so its letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
née is used before a married woman's maiden name to mean born

explanation.surface: A schemer born during a turbulent monarch's rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mastermind' reads as a noun for the schemer, but the answer is the verb: to mastermind a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to engineer a plan is to contrive and organise it, which is what a mastermind does.

clue.text: Supporters everywhere originally following game for free

parts.note: loo is an old card game

indicators.note: originally points to where each word begins, so only their opening letters count

parts.note: first letters of supporters and everywhere

explanation.surface: Fans everywhere chasing a match they can watch at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' places the initials after the card game, not before.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means unconfined or at liberty, the same as free when an animal gets out.

clue.text: Throw large cork

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British informal for toss or chuck
second meaning: a big stopper for a barrel or cask

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a casual British verb for tossing something and a noun for a stopper sealing a cask.

clue.text: Climber's staff's new pack stolen

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are put into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: all ten letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A mountaineer complains that their stick and new rucksack were stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 's means 'is': the staff is the anagram of the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpenstock is a long iron-tipped pole used by mountaineers, so a climber's staff.

clue.text: Communion plate close to priest is easily accessible

parts.note: a paten is the plate holding the bread at the Eucharist

indicators.note: the close of a word is where it ends, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of priest

explanation.surface: The communion plate near the priest can be reached easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like a phrase meaning near the priest, but it takes the word's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent means open and unobstructed, as of a passage or duct, hence plain and easily reached.

clue.text: Electronic facility storing President Eisenhower's first hearing aid

indicators.note: a thing storing goods keeps them inside it, so letters go within the word for facility

parts.note: E is the common abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
art means skill or knack, as does facility
Donald Trump, US President

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the name before it

parts.note: first letter of Eisenhower

explanation.surface: An electronic centre holding a famous US President's first hearing aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facility' looks like a building but means a knack or skill, and the President is the recent one, not Eisenhower, who supplies only an initial.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear trumpet is the old horn-shaped device held to the ear to help the hard of hearing.

clue.text: Note given to god containing Eastern European language

indicators.note: something containing another holds it inside, so a letter goes within the god's name

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
Eros is the Greek god of love
E is the abbreviation for Eastern
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A musical note offered to a deity, set in an Eastern European tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern European' reads as one phrase but splits into two separate E's.
explanation.definitionFit: Faeroese is the North Germanic tongue spoken in the Faeroe Islands, so a language.

clue.text: Philosopher dared to differ about spiritual education

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
to differ is to become unlike before, so the letters take another order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
RI is religious instruction, the old school subject

explanation.surface: A thinker bravely disagrees on how religion should be taught.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, was the name for religious education in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Derrida was the French thinker who founded deconstruction, a famous philosopher.

clue.text: Stop saving tin bottle

indicators.note: saving something keeps it safely held, so the word for tin is put inside

parts.note: to deter is to prevent or put off
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop keeping a tin bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a stoppered glass vessel into which wine or spirits are poured, a kind of bottle.

clue.text: Obsessive follower of celebrity carrying large sheath for knife

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it, so the following letters go inside

parts.note: a star is a famous person
L is the abbreviation for large

indicators.note: a sheath is the outer covering, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: outside letters of knife

explanation.surface: A celebrity's obsessive fan carrying a big knife holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of celebrity' tempts you to read the definition as a fan of a celebrity; 'of' is just the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalker is someone who persistently and obsessively pursues another person.

clue.text: Goes round Edgbaston's boundaries with five implements with which to hit ball

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its edges, so the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: outside letters of Edgbaston
V is the Roman numeral for five

parts.words: implements with which to hit ball
parts.note: irons are golf clubs

explanation.surface: A cricket scene at Edgbaston, Birmingham's Test ground, where boundaries are hit with five bats.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a boundary is a shot reaching the edge of the field; here the word means the word's edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Environ is a rare verb meaning to encircle or surround, so its third person singular means goes round.

clue.text: Poison made from wine containing slippery elm

indicators.note: a thing containing another holds it inside, so the rearranged tree goes within

parts.note: hock is a German white wine

indicators.note: something slippery slides about, so the letters slide into another order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A herbal poison brewed from wine with slippery elm bark in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Slippery elm is a real tree used in remedies, so the adjective seems to belong to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemlock is a highly toxic plant and the deadly drink made from it, famously given to Socrates.

clue.text: Clips are damaged in passage through rock

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: all eight letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: Climbing clips get damaged in a narrow passage through rock.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology a spiracle is a vent or tube formed in lava by escaping gas, a passage through stone.

clue.text: Honour priest with increase in wages

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for priest
a raise is a pay rise

explanation.surface: A priest is rewarded with a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone is to honour them with words of approval and admiration.

clue.text: Vegetable dip served after enjoyable starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening course, so only the opening letters of the word are used

parts.note: the first two letters of enjoyable
to dip is to plunge or dive

explanation.surface: A dinner party menu: a vegetable dip after some tasty appetisers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dip' and 'starters' both suggest party food, but the dip is a plunge and the starters are opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy salad plant of the chicory family, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Speyside's final label put on litre of the hard stuff

indicators.note: final means the end of the place name, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: last letter of Speyside
to label is to name
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: A Speyside distillery labels a litre bottle of whisky, the hard stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Speyside is a Scottish whisky region and 'the hard stuff' is slang for spirits, but here it means the hardest material in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body, and enamel paint dries to a hard glossy coat.

clue.text: Distinguished gathering admitting married woman with bug

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them in, so a letter goes inside the gathering

parts.note: a salon is a fashionable gathering of notable people
M is the abbreviation for married
Ella is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A smart party lets in a married woman who is carrying a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmonella is a bacterium causing food poisoning, and in everyday speech a bug is such a germ.

clue.text: Twisted gold wire for so-called precious gem

indicators.note: so-called refers to what something is called, which points to how a word is spoken

parts.note: a pearl is a precious gem from an oyster

explanation.definitionFit: Purl is a thread of twisted gold or silver wire used for embroidery and edging.

clue.text: Accumulate stakes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to combine resources into a common fund
second meaning: the total money bet by gamblers in a game

explanation.surface: Advice to a gambler: build up your bets.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to put resources together, and as a noun the combined bets in a game of chance.

clue.text: Kitchen utensil is returned by woman finally leaving flat

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: last letter of woman

explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman' tempts you towards EVE directly, but it supplies only N, which leaves EVEN to make EVE.

clue.text: Fabric from Greek island covering central section of colonnade

indicators.note: covering something wraps around it, so the island's name goes outside

parts.note: Crete is the largest Greek island

parts.note: the middle three letters of colonnade
